# Intake Brief: Easy editing of tutorial text (CG-0MUAVHX1D002J8HH)

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Feature**

## Problem statement

Main Street tutorial copy is already externalised out of gameplay code, but it lives in a **TypeScript source module** (`example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts`) whose values are wrapped in `tutorialKey(...)` / `modalKey(...)` / `overlayKey(...)` / `bankingHintKey(...)` expressions. Editing wording therefore requires opening a `.ts` file, understanding the key syntax, and risking a compile error — which is a barrier for the non-developer content/editorial writer who owns the copy. The producer wants all tutorial copy in a **CSV file that can be opened and edited in a spreadsheet**.

## Users

- **Non-developer content/editorial writer** — owns tutorial wording; must be able to edit it in a spreadsheet without touching TypeScript.
- **Developer/maintainer** — must be able to trust that a spreadsheet save cannot silently break the tutorial (missing/orphan/duplicate keys, mangled quoting, dropped placeholders).
- **Player** — must see the same (correct, data-driven) tutorial copy as today; this change is behaviour-preserving.

### Example user stories

- As a content editor, I want to open one CSV, edit the `text` column in my spreadsheet, save it, and have the tutorial use my wording after the normal build, so that I never need to understand TypeScript.
- As a developer, I want a build-time/CI test that validates the CSV (keys, duplicates, placeholders, quoting) so that a bad spreadsheet save cannot ship broken tutorial copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **CSV is the single source of tutorial copy.** All 62 tutorial strings — 26 step titles + 26 step bodies (`tutorial.T1..T26.title|body`), 4 offer-modal strings (`tutorial.modal.*`), 4 overlay button labels (`tutorial.overlay.*`), and 2 banking-hint strings (`tutorial.bankingHint.*`) — live in `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.csv` with a `key,text` header. No user-facing prose string literals remain in `tutorial-en.ts` (it holds only key helpers + the loader). *Metric: a test asserts `tutorial-en.csv` has a `key,text` header and exactly the 62 required keys; a grep/inspection confirms `tutorial-en.ts` contains no copy.*
2. **Loader preserves the public API.** `tutorial-en.ts` keeps exporting `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE`, `TUTORIAL_I18N_KEY_PREFIX`, `tutorialKey`, `modalKey`, `overlayKey`, and `bankingHintKey`, and builds `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE` from the CSV via a Vite `?raw` import + the core `parseCsv()` helper. All existing consumers (`TutorialFlow.ts`, overlay manager, tests) compile and pass **unchanged**. *Metric: existing `tutorial-i18n.test.ts`, `tutorial-text-updates.test.ts`, `tutorial-flow.test.ts` pass without edits.*
3. **CSV integrity is validated.** A test verifies: header is `key,text`; every required key is present; there are no duplicate or orphan/unknown keys; no value is empty; embedded commas round-trip; the embedded double quote in the banking hint (`"(1 banked)"`) round-trips; a leading UTF-8 BOM is tolerated (the loader strips it); and placeholder tokens (`{cardName}`, `{cost}`, `{bonus}`, `{synergyCardName}`) are preserved where expected. *Metric: new `tests/main-street/tutorial-csv.test.ts` all green.*
4. **Behaviour is preserved end-to-end.** `resolveTutorialStepText()` and `t()` resolve the same content as before the migration for every step (including data-driven card facts from `card-data.csv` and the modal/overlay/banking labels), with no raw `{token}` text leaking. *Metric: existing content assertions plus a full required-key parity assertion pass.*
5. **Documentation reflects the spreadsheet workflow.** `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` is updated so "Changing existing text" and "Adding a New Language" describe opening `tutorial-en.csv` in a spreadsheet, editing the `text` column, saving as CSV UTF-8 (quoting for embedded commas/quotes; keep placeholder tokens), and rebuilding. Any stale references to editing `tutorial-en.ts` are removed. *Metric: docs reviewed against the implemented workflow.*
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Bundle the CSV at build time via Vite `?raw` (no runtime `fetch`), matching `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts:13` (`./card-data.csv?raw`). A normal rebuild/redeploy is acceptable (producer Q3 = A).
- Use the existing core `parseCsv()` (`src/core-engine/CsvLoader.ts`) — no new runtime dependency. It already supports RFC4180 quoting: embedded commas, newlines, and escaped `""`.
- Preserve the i18n key scheme exactly (`tutorial.<STEP_ID>.<field>`, `tutorial.modal.*`, `tutorial.overlay.*`, `tutorial.bankingHint.*`).

## Failure Signature

- Test name: ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts — Last Round card: flips on the deck, settles at the resting position, and is omitted from its slot (waitForCondition timed out)
- Failing commit: latest `dev` at triage (root cause commit `21688987`, CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Failure screenshot: tests/coloretto/__screenshots__/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts/... omits from slot-1.png. check tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts:94:22 — Error: waitForCondition timed out. Seen during a full-suite run under heavy concurrent-agent CPU contention (load 25-49 on 16 cores); passes 26/26 in isolation at the same commit. discovered-from:CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA
```

## Root Cause

Not CPU-contention flakiness. The test now fails deterministically (~4 of 5 isolated runs at current `dev`).

Commit `21688987` (CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4) added `wholeRowValue()` and extended the Coloretto heuristic AI take gate to `netRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD OR wholeRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD` (`TAKE_THRESHOLD = 2`). A single bonus card has `wholeRowValue = BONUS_POINTS = 2`, so the AI now takes any row containing a bonus card.

In this test the AI's first turn may place a bonus card on a row (the session RNG defaults to `Math.random`, so the shuffled deck — and therefore the AI's first-turn card — varies run to run). After the human draws the Last Round card, the AI's final turn is then a TAKE, not a PLACE. The take animation (`playTakeAnimation`) uses flyers and never sets `flightCard`, so the test's fourth `waitForCondition` (`phase === 'animating' && flightCard !== null`) can never be satisfied; the round ends and phase becomes `round-scoring`.

Full investigation and evidence are recorded in the Plan-investigation comment.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout current `dev`: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test:
   `npx vitest run --project browser tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts -t "Last Round card"`
3. Repeat several times: the failure depends on whether the AI's first turn drew a bonus card.

## Impact

Blocks the Coloretto browser suite on `dev`. The AI change is intended behaviour; the test's assumption that the AI's final turn is a placement is the brittle part.

## Recommended Fix Direction

Make the test deterministic or action-agnostic, e.g.:

- Control `scene.session.rows` before the human's placement so the AI has no row worth taking (forces a place, preserving the existing flight-card assertions); and/or
- Treat the AI's final turn as either place or take and wait on the round transition rather than `flightCard`.

## Key Files

- `tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts`
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoAis.ts`
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts`

2. The test no longer depends on the AI's strategy choice or on a specific shuffled deck (no new flakiness under CPU contention).
3. Documentation is updated only if the fix changes documented behaviour; a test-only fix requires no doc change.
4. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

Card hover highlight in Lost Cities does not match the actual card size — it is too short vertically (top and bottom) because the tint overlay uses a hardcoded `CARD_H` (130px) instead of the game's `HAND_CARD_H` (137px).

## Problem

Lost Cities uses 100x137 card dimensions (`HAND_CARD_W`/`HAND_CARD_H`), but the shared `HandView` tint overlay system in `src/ui/HandView._setCardTint()` hardcodes `CARD_H` (130) as the overlay height. This means the hover highlight (green tint overlay) is 7px shorter than the actual card.

Additionally, Lost Cities does not pass `cardHeight` in its HandView construction options, so `this.cardHeight` also defaults to `CARD_H` (130).

## Root cause

| Location | What | Expected | Actual |
|----------|------|----------|--------|
| `src/ui/HandView.ts:1896` | Overlay height in `_setCardTint()` | `this.cardHeight` | `CARD_H` (130) |
| `LostCitiesRenderer.ts` HandView options | `cardHeight` option | `HAND_CARD_H` (137) | not passed (defaults to 130) |

Note: `this.cardWidth` is correctly set to `HAND_CARD_W` (100) via the HandView options, which is why the hover highlight width appears correct.

## Fix

1. **`src/ui/HandView.ts` line ~1896**: Change the overlay height from `CARD_H` to `this.cardHeight`
2. **`example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesRenderer.ts`**: Add `cardHeight: HAND_CARD_H` to the HandView construction options

## Acceptance Criteria

- Card hover highlight (green tint overlay) matches the card display size exactly — no visible gap at top/bottom
- All Lost Cities card types (numbered, investment, action) show consistent hover highlights
- Other games using HandView (Gym, Main Street, Golf, Sushi Go, Beleaguered Castle, Blackjack) are unaffected — hover highlights continue to work correctly
- Full project test suite passes

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `_setCardTint()` overlay creation (~line 1896)
- `src/ui/constants.ts` — `CARD_H` (130) default

## Problem statement

The Tableau Card Engine ships pre-1.0 builds (currently `v0.1.17`), but nothing in the UI signals that players are using an ALPHA build. Every game screen, the game-selector menu, and the Help/Settings panes should show a brightly coloured red **ALPHA** badge carrying the current version number, so users and testers always know they are on an unreleased ALPHA build.

## Users

- **Players / testers** — "When I open any game, I can immediately see that this is an ALPHA build and which version I'm on, so I know to report issues and can quote the exact version."
- **Release manager / producer** — "I can visually confirm from any screen that the deployed build is an ALPHA build and that the running version matches the release."
- **Developers** — "The badge is rendered by one shared helper, so adding a new game scene automatically gets the ALPHA banner with no per-game work."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A bright red **ALPHA** badge displaying the current version string (from `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`, i.e. the build-time `__APP_VERSION__`) is rendered **stacked above/over the title** on every Example Game scene and every Gym demo scene, delivered through the shared scene-title helper (`createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()`), so no per-game bespoke code is required. The one remaining bespoke title call site — `BlackjackScene`, which draws `'Blackjack'` with its own `scene.add.text` — is migrated to `createSceneTitle()` so no bespoke title rendering remains.
2. The same red ALPHA + version badge appears stacked above/over the one-off title on the Game Selector menu screen.
3. The SettingsPanel title shows the badge stacked above/over it, and HelpPanel gains a compact **"Help" + ALPHA badge** header at the top of its content (HelpPanel currently has no title heading).
4. The badge's version text equals `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`; the existing muted version labels on the menu (top-right) and settings (bottom-left) remain unchanged.
5. The badge renders correctly (legible, no clipping, no overlap with the top-left `Menu` button, the top-right HUD controls, or the existing version label) at the fixed 1280×720 design resolution used by every surface (`GAME_W` × `GAME_H`, `Phaser.Scale.FIT` with `CENTER_BOTH`); automated tests cover the shared badge helper and assert a badge showing `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` is created on each surface (Example Game / Gym header, Game Selector title, SettingsPanel title, HelpPanel header).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Shared-helper first.** All scene/game/Gym titles already route through `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()` (`src/ui/SceneHeader.ts`); extend those rather than patching individual scenes. The Game Selector title, `SettingsPanel` title, and `HelpPanel` header are separate one-off call sites.
- **Reuse the version source.** Do not access `__APP_VERSION__` directly — import the existing `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` / style constants from `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` so version handling stays in one place.
- **No new assets / permissive only.** Red badge must be drawn with Phaser primitives (rectangle + text); no new image assets, no new dependencies.
- **Do not remove existing version labels** (producer decision Q3a) — the badge is additive.
- **Reduced motion.** The badge is static (no animation), so it is inherently reduced-motion safe; do not add motion.
- **Canvas headroom.** Scene titles sit at `SCENE_HEADER_Y = 14`; a badge stacked *above* the title has little vertical room. Option (c) permits overlaying/overlapping the title's upper edge; the chosen geometry must remain legible and must not collide with the top-left `Menu` button or top-right HUD controls.
- **SLL requirement.** Positioning must respect the project's SLL/no-hardcoded-pixel rule where practical; the title helpers already own their fixed header geometry, so the badge should be defined relative to the title it decorates.

## Existing state

- `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` — `createSceneTitle()` (centred title at `GAME_W/2`, `SCENE_HEADER_Y = 14`) and `createSceneHeader()` (title + `Menu` button). Used by all Example Game renderers/scenes and `GymSceneBase.initHeader()`.
- `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` — `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` (`v<version>` from build-time `__APP_VERSION__`), `VERSION_COLOR`, `VERSION_ALPHA`, `VERSION_DEPTH`, `createVersionLabel()`.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — one-off bold title `'Tableau Card Engine'` at `(GAME_W/2, 30)` with a subtitle; version label already rendered top-right below the GitHub icon.
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — one-off `'Settings'` title at `(panelWidth/2, PADDING + 30)`.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — sections rendered in a scrollable content container; **no** title heading today.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSceneBase.ts` — `initHeader(title)` delegates to `createSceneHeader()`.

## Desired change

Add a shared `createAlphaBadge(scene, opts)` factory (in `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` or a new `src/ui/AlphaBadge.ts`) that renders a bright red badge containing `ALPHA` and `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`, positioned stacked above/over a given title (with an explicit anchor/y so callers control overlap). Wire it into `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()` by default (with an opt-out flag) so every Example Game and Gym scene inherits it, then add it explicitly to the Game Selector title, the SettingsPanel title, and a new compact HelpPanel header. Keep the existing muted version labels.

## Implementation order (test-first)

1. Extend `tests/ui/SceneHeader.test.ts` with failing unit tests for `createAlphaBadge()`: bright red fill, `ALPHA` + `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` text, anchor/overlap geometry relative to the decorated title, and the opt-out flag.
2. Add per-surface presence tests — `tests/ui/GameSelectorScene.test.ts`, `tests/ui/SettingsPanelVersion.browser.test.ts`, and a new `tests/ui/HelpPanel.test.ts`.
3. Implement `createAlphaBadge()` plus the default-on wiring in `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()`; export the factory and constants from `src/ui/index.ts`.
4. Wire the one-off surfaces (Game Selector title, SettingsPanel title, HelpPanel header) and migrate `BlackjackScene` to `createSceneTitle()`.
5. Update documentation (`docs/DEVELOPER.md` "Build-Time Version Injection" section, `README.md`) and code comments.
6. Verify: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/`, then the unit profile before any push (`npm test -- --project unit` + `npm run build`).


## Failure Classification (planning evidence, 2026-09-26)

**Classification: transient CPU-contention worker RPC timeout that Vitest surfaced as a failed file/test, which disables the existing retry mitigation and therefore fails the gate.**

Supporting evidence, all reproducible from this checkout:

1. **The retry mitigation never fired.** `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` emits
   `[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=1 outcome=failed args="--project unit"` in
   the recorded output — a single attempt. `runWithRetry` only retries when
   `shouldRetryOnce(output)` is true, and that masking guard requires an
   **all-files-passed** summary
   (`/Test Files\s+\d+\s+passed \(\d+\)/` plus no `failed` counts). This run
   reported `Test Files 1 failed | 416 passed (417)` and `Tests 1 failed`, so the
   guard returns false and the stage exits 1 without retrying.
2. **The guard gap is confirmed by direct predicate evaluation.** The runner's
   captured output is preserved at
   `.worklog/cache/02f9a2ba391d1da4493ebafa1cc63d4c/stdout.txt`. Evaluating the
   exported predicate against it:
   `shouldRetryOnce(<actual recorded output>) === false`, while the *same*
   output with only the two summary counts edited to the all-passed form
   (`Test Files 416 passed (416)` / `Tests 7164 passed | 8 skipped (7172)`)
   returns `true`. The sole difference between recovery and gate failure is
   Vitest counting the poisoned file as failed.
3. **The failure is not reproducible at either failing commit.**
   - **Same-commit proof (strongest):** occurrence 2 was on `933644bc` with a
     **418-file** corpus (`Test Files 1 failed | 417 passed (418)`,
     `Tests 1 failed | 7172 passed | 8 skipped (7181)`). Re-running the unit
     stage at that *same* commit ~60 minutes later produced
     `Test Files 418 passed (418)`,
     `Tests 7173 passed | 8 skipped (7181)`,
     `[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=0 outcome=clean args="--project unit"`.
     Identical commit, identical 418-file/7181-test corpus, one red run and one
     green run — the failure is non-deterministic, not a defect in the code
     under test.
   - **Corroborating proof:** `git show --name-status` confirms the only test
     changes since occurrence 1 (`a341ec3c`) are **additions**
     (`tests/main-street/pawn-shop-reputation.test.ts`, +8 unit tests) and one
     browser-test edit — no pre-existing unit test file was modified. Every unit
     test present at `a341ec3c` therefore also ran and passed at HEAD.
4. **Contention context.** Both poisoned attempts recorded collect ≈370s and
   tests ≈630-665s, against `collect 211.71s, tests 349.42s` on the clean
   re-run — roughly 1.8-1.9× — consistent with concurrent suites competing for
   CPU on the same host. This is the documented transient class from
   CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3, CG-0MSCI73RH004VPCE and CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N.

| Run | Commit | Outcome | Test Files | Tests | collect/tests | `[vitest-runner]` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (incident) | `a341ec3c` | red | 1 failed \| 416 passed (417) | 1 failed \| 7164 passed \| 8 skipped | 371.18s / 665.35s | `attempts=1 status=1 outcome=failed` |
| 2 (incident) | `933644bc` | red | 1 failed \| 417 passed (418) | 1 failed \| 7172 passed \| 8 skipped | 369.62s / 631.88s | `attempts=1 status=1 outcome=failed` |
| 3 (re-run) | `933644bc` | **green** | 418 passed (418) | 7173 passed \| 8 skipped | 211.71s / 349.42s | `attempts=1 status=0 outcome=clean` |

**Discriminator resolved for the sibling item:** CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU (the same
signature, previously mitigated) recorded that it could not tell whether the
poisoned run was the only attempt or the retry. Both occurrences here report
`attempts=1`, which answers that: on these recurrences the run was the **only**
attempt, because the transient presented with a failed-file summary and
therefore never qualified for a retry. The previous mitigation covers the
*all-passed* variant of the transient; these recurrences expose the
*failed-file* variant, which the masking guard cannot distinguish from a genuine
failure. `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`'s `tail -20` also means the console log names
neither the failed file nor a distinct assertion, so the failure is only
diagnosable from the runner's summary line — see the evidence gap below.

### Evidence gap (closed by the approved scope)

`scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` pipes each stage through `tail -20`, so the persisted
output does not name the failing test/file and does not show whether Vitest
reported a distinct assertion error alongside the worker-timeout unhandled
error. We therefore could not tell whether the counted failure was *purely* the
`onTaskUpdate` timeout artefact or a real test that also exceeded its own
timeout under the same contention. **Producer decision (2026-09-26): remove the
truncation** so the next recurrence is fully diagnosable — see AC7.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout a341ec3c2d92bca48035e7d09ca1fec24da726c0`
2. Run the failing stage: `npm --silent test` (Vitest via `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`; there is no pytest suite in this repository).
   To reproduce the unit stage alone: `npx tsx scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project unit`
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item — in particular the `[vitest-runner]` summary line (attempts/outcome) and the identity of any failed test file, neither of which survives the `tail -20` truncation in the excerpt above.

## Impact

The unit stage of the full suite exits 1 although every test passes on re-run,
so the release/push gate fails spuriously and must be retried manually. This is
the second recurrence of this transient class (after CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU) and it
blocks PR creation for the agent's current work item whenever it fires. It is
currently live: occurrence 2 was observed on `dev` HEAD `933644bc` at
18:08:03Z, and the same commit's re-run was green — so the gate can fail at any
time under host CPU contention, with no code change involved.

**Note:** triage also surfaced a *distinct* latent defect while investigating —
`tests/golf/replay.test.ts` is not self-contained and fails under a bare
`npx vitest run --project unit` (it needs `GAMES_CONFIG=full`, which only
`scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` exports). It is **not** this failure (it would report
4 failed tests, not 1) and has been filed separately as
**CG-0MUIRPUX9003T24V**, discovered-from this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Root cause closed, not bypassed (approach (a), producer-confirmed 2026-09-26):** the retry mitigation recovers from a worker RPC timeout that Vitest reports *as a failed file*, while still refusing to retry or accept a genuine per-file assertion failure that merely coincides with the transient signature. The mitigation attributes the reported failures: only when every reported failure is the worker-timeout signature itself may the run be treated as transient (retry once; accept if the retry is again purely transient). *Verified by:* extended unit tests in `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` covering (a) a transient signature with a failed-file summary attributable only to the timeout — which must be retried/accepted — and (b) a genuine assertion failure alongside the signature — which must still be refused. The existing conservative cases in that file must remain passing.
- **The recorded failing run becomes a regression fixture:** the predicate is exercised against the real captured output of this incident (or an equivalent verbatim excerpt) so the recurrence cannot silently return. *Verified by:* a test in `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` that asserts the incident-shaped output is treated as transient while a genuine failure bearing the same signature is not.
- **Failure classification recorded with evidence:** the transient signature is confirmed non-reproducible via a green re-run whose `[vitest-runner]` line shows `status=0`, and the mechanism that defeated the retry is demonstrated from the recorded output. *Status: met by this planning session* — see *Failure Classification* above.
- **Gate verified green:** `npm --silent test` (or, at minimum, its unit stage) exits 0 at `dev` HEAD — and, because this is a non-deterministic contention flake, the AC is satisfied by demonstrating a green stage together with the mitigation's recovery path rather than by a single green run. *Verified by:* the `[vitest-runner]` summary line (`status=0`, plus any `retry-clean`/`accepted-transient` outcome under contention) together with a run in which a synthetic transient-with-failed-file input is recovered.
- **CI stage output is no longer truncated (producer-confirmed 2026-09-26):** no stage of `npm test` in `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` pipes its output through `tail -20` (or, if bounded, persists the full untruncated output), so a recurrence names the failed test/file and shows any distinct assertion error alongside the transient signature. The trailing `[vitest-runner] attempts=… status=… outcome=…` summary line is still emitted. *Verified by:* reading the pipeline in `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` (no `tail` truncation on the unit/browser/tutorial/electron-smoke stages) and by a run whose output contains the failed-file detail. Stale comments referencing the truncation (`scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` module docstring, `scripts/run-electron-smoke.sh`, `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` section comment) are updated or removed.
- **Shared truncation pattern reconciled:** the same `tail -20` pattern in `scripts/run-smoke-tests.sh` and `scripts/run-dev-tests.sh` is either aligned with the CI runner or explicitly recorded as a follow-up work item. *Verified by:* the diff or the recorded follow-up id.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the change, including the CPU-contention mitigation section of `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, the retry-guard rationale in `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`'s module docstring, and the quality-gate wording in `AGENTS.md` if the accepted-run semantics change.
- **Full project test suite passes with the new changes.**

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — `shouldRetryOnce()` masking guard and `runWithRetry()`; the site of the gap.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — guard predicate coverage; must be extended with the incident-shaped case (and its truncation section comment updated).
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — stage wiring, `--timeout-ms` bounds, and the `tail -20` truncation to remove (AC7).
- `scripts/run-smoke-tests.sh` — the same `tail -20` pattern (AC8: align or record a follow-up).
- `scripts/run-dev-tests.sh` — the same `tail -20` pattern (AC8: align or record a follow-up).
- `scripts/run-electron-smoke.sh` — comment explaining its summary line survives the CI wrapper's truncation; stale once AC7 lands.
- `vite.config.ts` — `unit` project `maxWorkers: 4` CPU-contention cap.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — CPU-contention mitigation and test-profile documentation.
- `.worklog/cache/02f9a2ba391d1da4493ebafa1cc63d4c/stdout.txt` — the recorded failing-run output used as evidence/fixture source.

## Proposed approach

**Decision (producer, 2026-09-26):** approach **(a) attribution-aware retry**,
plus removing the CI stage truncation. Approach (b) is **rejected**.

- **(a) Attribution-aware retry — CONFIRMED.** When the transient signature is
  present *and* the summary reports failures, attribute the failures: if every
  reported failure is the worker-timeout signature itself (no distinct
  assertion/original error), treat the run as transient — retry once, and accept
  if the retry is again purely transient. A distinct assertion failure keeps the
  guard refusing, exactly as today. This requires the runner to inspect the
  failure section rather than only the summary counts. This preserves the
  documented "never mask a genuine failure" guarantee.
- **(b) Unconditional retry-once on the signature — REJECTED.** Retrying
  whenever the signature appears (using the last attempt's result) would let a
  genuinely flaky failure pass on retry, weakening the documented masking
  guarantee and the deliberate test at
  `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts:87` ("returns false when the
  timeout signature is present alongside genuine file failures").

**Confirmed hardening (AC7):** `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` no longer pipes stage
output through `tail -20`, so a future recurrence names the poisoned file and
shows whether a distinct assertion accompanied the timeout. Removing the
truncation also makes the runner's end-of-output `[vitest-runner]` summary line
non-load-bearing, so the comments that explain their survival purpose must be
updated rather than left stale.

**Order (test-first):** extend `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` with
the incident-shaped case and confirm it fails against the current predicate,
then change the predicate — per the project's test-first discipline. The change
must be small enough to read as one function's contract, not a rewrite of the
runner.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

- Discovered item: CG-0MUIRPUX9003T24V (golf replay test hermeticity)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Research findings (no producer interview was required for this item)

- **Q: Is the reported failure reproducible at the failing commit?**
  **Answer (research, this session): No — proven at the same commit.** The unit
  stage was re-run green at `dev` HEAD `933644bc` (`Test Files 418 passed (418)`,

  outcome=clean`) while incident occurrence 2 on the *same* commit reported
  `Test Files 1 failed | 417 passed (418)` and `Tests 1 failed | 7172 passed |
  8 skipped` — the same 418-file / 7181-test corpus, red then green. The commits
  since occurrence 1 only *added* tests
  (`tests/main-street/pawn-shop-reputation.test.ts`, +8 unit tests) and edited a
  browser test; `git show --name-status` confirms no pre-existing unit test file
  was modified, so every unit test at `a341ec3c` also ran and passed at HEAD.
- **Q: Why did the retry mitigation not recover either run?**
  **Answer (research, this session): because `shouldRetryOnce()` requires an
  all-files-passed summary.** Evaluated against the recorded occurrence-1 output
  it returns `false`; evaluated against the same output with only the summary
  counts edited to the all-passed form it returns `true`. Both occurrences
  report `attempts=1`, confirming no retry was attempted. Evidence:
  `.worklog/cache/02f9a2ba391d1da4493ebafa1cc63d4c/stdout.txt`, the triage-bot
  comment recording occurrence 2, and `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`.
- **Q: Is `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` (which fails locally) the reported failure?**
  **Answer (research, this session): No.** Without `GAMES_CONFIG=full` it reports
  **4** failed tests, whereas both incidents reported **1**; `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  exports `GAMES_CONFIG=full`, so it passes in the reported path. Filed separately
  as CG-0MUIRPUX9003T24V (discovered-from this item).
- **Q: Was the earlier sibling item's open discriminator ("was the poisoned run
  the only attempt, or the retry?") resolvable?**
  **Answer (research, this session): yes — it was the only attempt, in both

- **Q: Which mitigation should be adopted — attribution-aware retry (a) or unconditional retry-once on the signature (b)?** — **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-26): (a).** Final: **approach (a) attribution-aware retry**; (b) rejected. # Decision: merge the core into `Tableau-Card-Engine` (Option A)

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer I can work on the engine, the Gym, the launcher shell and the
distribution in **one repository** (`Tableau-Card-Engine`), while each game is
still developed and released independently in its own repository
(`tce-<game>`) that composes `Tableau-Card-Engine` as its `./core` submodule —
so that there is exactly one "core" repo, the ownership of the launcher is
unambiguous, and the multi-game distribution composes the game repos as
**sibling checkouts** without any submodule cycle.

## Decision (Option A — accepted)

1. `Tableau-Card-Engine` becomes the **single merged engine + launcher core**:
   engine modules (`src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`,
   `src/ui`, `src/ai`, `src/balance-cards`), the **Gym** (`example-games/gym`),
   the launcher shell (`GameSelectorScene`, `createCardGame`), `main.ts`,
   `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `configs/`, the Electron host (`electron/`)
   and shared assets all live here. It carries **no games** at HEAD
   (`example-games/` holds only `gym`).
2. Each `tce-<game>` repository composes `Tableau-Card-Engine` as its `./core`
   **git submodule** (URL `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine.git`)
   and keeps its own source at repo-root `src/`.
3. The multi-game distribution is composed from the **same** repo plus the game
   repos checked out as **siblings** (`../tce-<game>`) — the mechanism the
   discovery plugin already supports (`configs/*.json` `path` +
   `siblingScenePath`). `Tableau-Card-Engine` has **no game `.gitmodules`**.
4. `tableau-card-engine-core` is **retired** (archived, then deleted once no
   reference remains).

## The cycle constraint (why games are siblings, not submodules)

If `Tableau-Card-Engine` submoduled the games **and** the games submodule
`Tableau-Card-Engine`, the dependency graph would be circular
(`tce-golf → core → Tableau-Card-Engine → tce-golf → …`). Cyclic submodules
break `--recurse-submodules` and most tooling. Therefore the distribution
composes the game repos as siblings, exactly as the architecture already
documents ("composition is sibling directories, not git submodules").

Consequence accepted: a full distribution checkout is no longer a single
`git clone --recurse-submodules`; it is the core repo plus sibling game clones,
which the plan should automate with a small bootstrap manifest/script.

## Why not the alternatives

- **Thin distribution (separate `Tableau-Card-Engine` that submodules core +
   games).** This is today's three-way split. It keeps a second launcher-capable
   repo (`tableau-card-engine-core`) whose ownership overlaps the launcher, and
   it is what created the "which repo owns `main.ts`/`vite.config.ts`/`configs`"
   ambiguity in the first place. Rejected as unnecessarily duplicative.
- **Engine as an npm package.** Games would `npm install` the engine and the
   launcher could freely submodule games (no cycle). Cleaner for versioning, but
   it contradicts the project's submodule model and would require npm
   publication, which is explicitly out of scope.

## Current state (starting point)

- Public remotes exist: `tableau-card-engine-core` (engine + Gym + launcher
  shell, no games), `tce-<game>` ×8, and the original `Tableau-Card-Engine`
  monorepo which **still carries the in-tree games** and has no `.gitmodules`.
- The 8 game repos' `.gitmodules` currently point `core` at
  `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core.git`, pinned to a
  filtered-history commit. Those pins do **not** exist in
  `Tableau-Card-Engine`, so the repoint must also re-pin to a
  `Tableau-Card-Engine` commit.
- `Tableau-Card-Engine` already contains the complete engine + launcher history,
  so no core re-extraction is needed — only the games are extracted out.

## Migration plan (for decomposition by `/skill:plan`)

1. Land the decision record (`docs/dev/`) and update the multi-repo docs.
2. Re-partition `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`: the `core` target becomes
   `Tableau-Card-Engine`; remove the `tableau-card-engine-core` target; games
   unchanged.
3. Update `scripts/extract-repos.sh`, `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` and
   `scripts/publish-repos.ts` for the new core name/URL.
4. Remove the in-tree games from `Tableau-Card-Engine` HEAD; make the launcher
   resolve games only as siblings.
5. Repoint each `tce-<game>` `./core` URL to `Tableau-Card-Engine` and re-pin
   the gitlink to a `Tableau-Card-Engine` commit; commit and push each.
6. Archive and then delete `tableau-card-engine-core`.
7. Update README/DEVELOPER/AGENTS; add a bootstrap manifest/script for a full
   sibling distribution checkout.
8. Verify fresh clones and the full build/test gates; record evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `Tableau-Card-Engine` HEAD contains no `example-games/<game>` (only `gym`)
   and can build `core-only`, `solo` and `full` presets using sibling game
   checkouts.
2. `Tableau-Card-Engine` contains no game `.gitmodules`; the distribution
   composition is sibling-only, with no submodule cycle.
3. Every `tce-<game>` `.gitmodules` records
   `core = git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine.git`; a fresh
   `git clone --recurse-submodules` of each game repo has a clean
   `git submodule status`.
4. A fresh recursive clone of `tce-golf` and `tce-main-street` installs,
   builds and passes `npm test -- --project unit`.
5. `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build` succeeds from `Tableau-Card-Engine` with
   the game repos present as siblings.
6. `tableau-card-engine-core` is archived/deleted and no doc, script, preset or
   `.gitmodules` references it.
7. The decision record is committed under `docs/dev/` and
   `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` reflects the merged-core reality; no
   documentation contradicts it.
8. The full project test suite passes at the final commit; no regression in the
   launcher, Gym or distribution builds.

## Constraints

- The submodule graph must stay acyclic (games submodule the core; the core
  never submodules games).
- No history rewrite of `Tableau-Card-Engine`; the migration is additive at
  HEAD (game files remain in history, which is accepted).
- Push to `dev` only; `main` is promoted by the ship skill.
- `tableau-card-engine-core` is public — retire it only after all references are
  removed.

## Risks

- Repointing/re-pinning 8 repos is fiddly and easy to get half-done.
- Losing the one-command distribution clone (mitigate with a bootstrap
  manifest/script).
- Games' `./core` now pulls the whole launcher/distribution (heavier checkout;
  accepted).
- Per-game CI and where game work-items live remain undefined and should be
  tracked separately.

## Out of scope

- npm publication of the engine.
- Per-game CI pipelines and the per-game Worklog strategy (separate items).
- Scrubbing game files from `Tableau-Card-Engine` history.
- Changes to the engine/Gym/game behaviour itself (this is a repository-topology
  and tooling change only).
